extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates / graduate students and researchers studying Sobolev spaces and elliptic boundary value problems
extracted.subtask_description: Theory and useful criteria for existence, uniqueness, regularity, maximum principles, spectral decomposition, and related inequalities for second-order elliptic PDEs and Sobolev spaces; includes variational and alternative solution methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local elliptic regularity (H^{m+2} gain)
rubrics_metrics.description: If u ∈ H^1(Ω) solves ∇u·∇ϕ = fϕ for all ϕ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω) and f ∈ H^m(Ω), then θu ∈ H^{m+2}(Ω) for every θ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω). In particular f ∈ C^∞(Ω) ⇒ u ∈ C^∞(Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The result is proved by induction on m; regularity is local (depends only on f locally). For very weak solutions u ∈ L^2 one can obtain the same conclusion by more delicate arguments (see Agmon).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypoellipticity (local smoothness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularity of u|_ω depends only on regularity of f|_ω: e.g., f ∈ C^∞(ω) implies u ∈ C^∞(ω) even if f is irregular outside ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expresses hypoellipticity for elliptic operators; use local regularity arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum principle for the Dirichlet problem (Theorem 9.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume f ∈ L^2(Ω) and u ∈ H^1(Ω) ∩ C(Ω) satisfy ∇u·∇ϕ + uϕ = fϕ for all ϕ ∈ H^1_0(Ω). Then for all x ∈ Ω, min{inf_{∂Ω} u, inf_Ω f} ≤ u(x) ≤ max{sup_{∂Ω} u, sup_Ω f}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via Stampacchia truncation method with suitable C^1 truncation G; can remove continuity assumption in many cases using trace theory. Corollaries give positivity preservation and L^∞ bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: positivity and L^∞ bounds (Corollary 9.28)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases: if f=0 then ||u||_{L^∞(Ω)} ≤ ||u||_{L^∞(∂Ω)}; if u=0 on ∂Ω then ||u||_{L^∞(Ω)} ≤ ||f||_{L^∞(Ω)}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical maximum-principle pointwise argument (Remark 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: For classical solutions in bounded smooth domains, maxima occur on the boundary; at an interior maximum ∇u=0 and second derivatives ≤0 so -Δu ≤ 0 and comparison with f yields the bound u(x0) ≤ f(x0) ≤ K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method applies to general second-order elliptic equations after diagonalizing the coefficient matrix at the extremum; proof is more delicate for weak solutions (see Gilbarg–Trudinger).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum principle with rough coefficients (Proposition 9.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a_{ij} ∈ L^∞(Ω) satisfy ellipticity, a_i, a_0 ∈ L^∞(Ω) with a_0 ≥ 0, and u ∈ H^1(Ω)∩C(Ω) satisfies the weak form (78), then [u ≥ 0 on ∂Ω and f ≥ 0 in Ω] ⇒ [u ≥ 0 in Ω].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variants: if a_0≡0 and Ω bounded then f ≤ 0 ⇒ u ≤ sup_{∂Ω} u; if f=0 then inf_{∂Ω} u ≤ u ≤ sup_{∂Ω} u. Proof uses truncation G and energy estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum principle for the Neumann problem (Proposition 9.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ L^2(Ω) and u ∈ H^1(Ω) satisfies ∇u·∇ϕ + uϕ = fϕ for all ϕ ∈ H^1(Ω) (Neumann type weak formulation), then for a.e. x ∈ Ω, inf_Ω f ≤ u(x) ≤ sup_Ω f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to Dirichlet maximum principle; proof follows same ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of eigenfunctions and spectral decomposition (Theorem 9.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist a Hilbert basis (e_n)_{n≥1} of L^2(Ω) and λ_n>0 with λ_n→+∞ such that e_n ∈ H^1_0(Ω)∩C^∞(Ω) and -Δ e_n = λ_n e_n in Ω (Dirichlet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct via the solution operator T: L^2→L^2 (Dirichlet inverse of -Δ) which is compact self-adjoint; eigenfunctions are smooth inside Ω by local regularity; eigenvalues λ_n = 1/μ_n with μ_n eigenvalues of T.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert basis in H^1_0 with scaled eigenfunctions (Remark 28)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence (e_n / √λ_n) is an orthonormal Hilbert basis of H^1_0(Ω) with respect to the scalar product (u,v) ↦ ∫(∇u·∇v + uv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One must check density in H^1_0 and use eigenfunction orthogonality; regularity yields membership in H^m locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is connected, class C^1, and 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, then ∃C such that ||u -  ar u||_{L^p} ≤ C ||∇u||_{L^p} for all u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω), where  ar u is the average of u on Ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used together with Sobolev inequalities to derive further estimates; constant depends on domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardy's inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is bounded of class C^1 and 1 < p < ∞, setting d(x)=dist(x,∂Ω) there exists C with ||u/d||_{L^p} ≤ C ||∇u||_{L^p} for all u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(Ω). Conversely, if u∈W^{1,p}(Ω) and (u/d)∈L^p(Ω) then u∈W^{1,p}_0(Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for boundary singularity control; see Lions–Magenes for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gagliardo–Nirenberg interpolation inequalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Various interpolation inequalities: e.g., if u ∈ L^p∩W^{2,r} then u ∈ W^{1,q} with 1/q = 1/2(1/p + 1/r) and ||Du||_{L^q} ≤ C ||u||_{W^{2,r}}^{1/2} ||u||_{L^p}^{1/2}.  Particular cases yield e.g. W^{2,r}∩L^∞ is an algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many concrete instances are given (p=∞ ⇒ q=2r; p=q=r ⇒ estimate splitting Du bound into ε||D^2u|| + C_ε||u||). Use to control nonlinearities and product spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpolation inequality in 2D (Example used frequently)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used often in PDE estimates where L^4 norms appear (nonlinearities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other interpolation inequalities (Example 3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when embedding into L^p via higher integrability of derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fractional Sobolev spaces W^{s,p} and H^s
rubrics_metrics.description: For 0<s<1 and 1≤p<∞ define W^{s,p}(Ω) as functions u∈L^p with (u(x)-u(y))/|x-y|^{s+N/p} ∈ L^p(Ω×Ω); set H^s = W^{s,2}. For non-integer s=m+σ define via derivatives D^α u ∈ W^{σ,p}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These spaces are interpolation spaces between L^p and W^{1,p}; also definable via Fourier transform when Ω=R^N and p=2. They are central in trace theory and fractional regularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace theorem and Lemma 9.9
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a bounded linear trace operator u↦u|_{∂Ω} mapping W^{1,p}(Ω) to W^{1-1/p,p}(∂Ω); it is surjective and its kernel is W^{1,p}_0(Ω). For Ω=R^N_+ a direct inequality bounds ||u(·,0)||_{L^p(R^{N-1})} by ||u||_{W^{1,p}(R^N_+)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace operator extends by density; use Lemma 9.9 for the half-space and local charts for general domains. Important for giving boundary values meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green's formula and boundary normal derivative mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: For u,v ∈ H^1(Ω) one has ∫_Ω ∂u/∂x_i v = -∫_Ω u ∂v/∂x_i + ∫_{∂Ω} u v n_i dσ (surface integral meaningful as u,v ∈ L^2(∂Ω)). For u ∈ W^{2,p}(Ω), ∂u/∂n ∈ W^{1-1/p,p}(∂Ω) and Green's formula holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The map u↦{u|_{∂Ω}, ∂u/∂n} is bounded, linear and surjective from W^{2,p}(Ω) onto W^{2-1/p,p}(∂Ω)×W^{1-1/p,p}(∂Ω).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operators of order 2m and elliptic systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence and regularity results extend to elliptic operators of order 2m and elliptic systems; an essential ingredient is Gårding's inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum principle does not generally extend except in special cases. See Agmon, Lions–Magenes, Agmon–Douglis–Nirenberg for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agmon–Douglis–Nirenberg L^p regularity (Theorem 9.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is class C^2 with bounded boundary and 1<p<∞, then for f∈L^p(Ω) there exists a unique u∈W^{2,p}(Ω)∩W^{1,p}_0(Ω) solving -Δu+u=f, and ||u||_{W^{2,p}} ≤ C ||f||_{W^{0,p}}. If Ω is C^{m+2} and f∈W^{m,p} then u∈W^{m+2,p} with estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach uses explicit representation and Calderón–Zygmund singular integral theory; result fails for p=1 and p=∞.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schauder C^{2,α} regularity (Theorem 9.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is bounded of class C^{2,α} and f∈C^{0,α}(Ω) (0<α<1) then there exists unique u∈C^{2,α}(Ω) solving -Δu+u=f with Dirichlet data u=0 on ∂Ω. Higher regularity: if Ω and f are C^{m+2,α},C^{m,α} then u∈C^{m+2,α}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses explicit representation and singular integral theory in Hölder spaces; alternative approaches by Campanato/Stampacchia avoid singular integrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: De Giorgi–Nash–Stampacchia Hölder regularity (Theorem 9.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω bounded regular, a_{ij}∈L^∞(Ω) satisfy ellipticity, f∈L^p(Ω) with p>N/2, and u∈H^1_0(Ω) solves weakly a_{ij}∂_i u ∂_j ϕ = fϕ, then u∈C^{0,α}(Ω) for some 0<α<1 depending on Ω, a_{ij}, p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives interior Hölder continuity even with merely bounded measurable coefficients; see Stampacchia, Gilbarg–Trudinger for proofs and estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of the variational method and duality extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Variational method fails for data f∈L^1(Ω) or Radon measures because the linear functional ϕ↦∫ fϕ is not defined on H^1_0. Use duality: extend the solution operator T:L^2→L^2 to T*: M(Ω)→L^p(Ω) (p>N/2) to obtain very weak/generalized solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For f∈L^1, u=T^* f ∈ L^q for all q< N/(N-2); u satisfies the PDE in a very weak sense with test functions in C^2_c(Ω).

rubrics_metrics.name: Density method for Dirichlet data (Theorem 9.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: If g∈C(∂Ω) and Ω regular bounded, there exists a unique u∈C(Ω)∩C^∞(Ω) solving -Δu+u=0 in Ω with u=g on ∂Ω. Construct by approximating g by smooth boundary data and passing to the limit using maximum principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires enough smoothness of Ω; Perron method gives an alternative construction via supremum of subsolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hopf strong maximum principle (Theorem 9.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let u∈C(Ω)∩C^2(Ω) satisfy -∂_j(a_{ij}∂_i u) + a_i ∂_i u + a_0 u = f in Ω with f≥0 and coefficients regular; if there exists x_0∈Ω with u(x_0)=min_Ω u and u(x_0)≤0 then u is constant in Ω (and f=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothesis u(x_0) ≤ 0 unnecessary if a_0=0. Use Hopf boundary point lemma and strong maximum principle proofs in classical references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positivity alternative (Corollary 9.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: If u∈C(Ω)∩C^2(Ω) satisfies the equation with f≥0 in Ω and u≥0 on ∂Ω then either u>0 in Ω or u≡0 in Ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence of the strong maximum principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectral properties: simplicity of first eigenvalue and positivity
rubrics_metrics.description: For -Δ (or more general elliptic A) with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary on a connected bounded regular domain, the first eigenvalue λ_1 is simple and the associated eigenfunction e_1 can be chosen strictly positive in Ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from Krein–Rutman theorem and maximum principle; asymptotic behavior λ_n ∼ c n^{2/N} when n→∞.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degenerate elliptic problems (condition and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems where a_{ij} do not satisfy uniform ellipticity but only a_{ij}(x) ξ_i ξ_j ≥ 0 for all ξ; such degenerate operators require different techniques and references (Kohn–Nirenberg, Oleinik–Radkevitch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum principle and regularity theory change substantially; consult specialized literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories and techniques for nonlinear elliptic problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonlinear elliptic PDEs include semilinear (−Δu = f(x,u)), quasilinear (coefficients depend on u and ∇u), fully nonlinear (F(x,u,Du,D^2u)=0), and free-boundary problems. Techniques include monotonicity methods, topological fixed-point and degree theories, variational critical point methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and major references provided (Browder, Krasnoselskii, Rabinowitz, Ambrosetti–Prodi, Zeidler). Choose method depending on structure: monotone, variational, or topological.
